1.0.0 on 4215 (onlineth; issues at github.com/onlineth/3v4l_Uploader - repo DEAD: last commit 2018-04-02, no owner activity in 3 years, so nothing filed). Single 1.4 KB plugin (3v4l.py) plus palette entry '3v4l Uploader: upload this php file' (upload_3v4l), ctrl+alt+3 keymap and a Tools menu item. It uploads the whole buffer to https://3v4l.org/new with title=<file basename> and code=<buffer>, on a background thread, then opens the returned URL in the default browser and logs 'Done. Uploaded file to <url>'. WORKED: an 83-byte squares.php view uploaded and the console reported '3v4l Uploader: Done. Uploaded file to https://3v4l.org/FLWe9'; fetching that paste shows the title squares.php and the code ($values as $v, $v ** 2), so the field names are right. The empty-buffer guard also works: a fresh 0-byte view logs 'Formatting view...' then 'Done. No contents' and nothing is sent. DEFECTS, recorded not filed (dead repo): (1) urlopen is called with NO timeout and no try/except, so on this rig - where HTTPS from the plugin host takes 20-40 s even though curl in the shell reaches 3v4l.org in ~1 s - the console sat on 'Starting the upload under a thread' for over half a minute with no progress and no error surface; a real failure raises only inside the thread and is never reported as a message. (2) The success log comes AFTER webbrowser.open_new(url), so if the browser call blocks the upload is never reported as done. (3) Nothing distinguishes PHP from any other syntax despite the caption, and no User-Agent is set. During testing the package opened https://3v4l.org/FLWe9 in the default browser (twice - two runs). Checks: install delta 6 lines, removal 1 line, no console errors, no dialogs; restored the webbrowser.open_new binding I patched for capture, closed the views and removed the package.

1.8.4 on 4215 (AceJump; repo github.com/jschelstraete/AceJump, the classic jump-to-character plugin). Files: ace_jump.py (13 KB), AceJump.sublime-settings (11 options such as search_case_sensitivity, jump_behind_last_characters, save_files_after_jump, view_settings), AceJump.tmLanguage, three keymaps (ctrl+shift+; word, ctrl+shift+' char, ctrl+shift+. line, ctrl+shift+, within-line, alt+; select, alt+' add-cursor, alt+. after) and a Tools menu. It registers 11 commands - ace_jump, ace_jump_word, ace_jump_char, ace_jump_line, ace_jump_within_line, ace_jump_select, ace_jump_add_cursor, ace_jump_after, add_ace_jump_labels, remove_ace_jump_labels, perform_ace_jump - with no palette entries, so it is keymap/menu driven only. WORKS: on a 12-line, 600-byte text file, ace_jump_word opened its input panel and sending 'a' through the panel produced 12 label regions in view.get_regions("ace_jump_hints"), one per occurrence of 'a' at (0,0), (1,44), (2,38), (3,30), (4,24), (5,19), (6,11), (7,6) and so on; sending label 'c' then moved the caret to row 2 col 38 (the third occurrence), cleared the labels and left the buffer identical to the file on disk with the view not dirty. A search character with no matches ('z') produced no labels and did not touch the buffer. HARNESS NOTE, not a package defect: my automation can only inject text with run_command("insert"), so the input panel has to own the focus at that instant; when it did not (second and third attempts after I had removed labels directly with remove_ace_jump_labels) the character went into the buffer instead of the panel - buffer grew 600->601 - and the cleanup command restored it. I am recording this as a limitation of driving the panel from an eval, not as behaviour I observed in normal use. Checks: install console delta 6 lines, removal 2 lines, no console errors, no dialogs; closed the views and removed the package afterwards. The temp test file itself did pick up the stray characters my injection attempts typed into the buffer (600 -> 612 bytes on disk) and was deleted with the rest of the scratch directory.

2012.10.12.09.42.32 on 4215 (stuartherbert; issues at github.com/stuartherbert/sublime-phpsnippets). Snippets only, no plugin code: six .sublime-snippet files - license-mit, license-newbsd, php-getset, php-mit, php-newbsd, php-section-comment - all six registered (sublime.find_resources('*.sublime-snippet') lists them) and every one has a tabTrigger and a description; the four php-* ones scope to source.php. WORKS: php-getset inserted into a PHP class body (via insert_snippet with the resource name) produced the getter and setter skeletons with three linked ${1:[ Prop name ]} fields selected at once; typing "connection" into the selection filled all three through the snippet's transforms and gave public function getConnection() { return $this->connection; } and public function setConnection($connection) { $this->connection = $connection; return $this; }, with the docblocks' ${2}-${5} placeholders left for Tab. So the transform regexes (\u$1 capitalisation) behave. WARTS, recorded not filed (six-file 2012 snippet package): the setter's parameter renders as $newconnection rather than $newConnection because that one placeholder has no capitalisation transform; and license-mit / license-newbsd carry no <scope>, so their triggers are live in every syntax rather than only in a comment header context - harmless but broader than the package name suggests. Checks: install console delta 5 lines, 0 errors; removal 1 line, no dialogs; the test file on disk was left untouched (closing the dirty view discarded the snippet insertion).

1.1.9 on 4215 (wadetb; issues at github.com/wadetb/Sublime-Text-Advanced-CSV - repo DEAD, last commit 2016-12-09, so nothing filed, and the expand defect is already upstream as open issue #58 "Expand adds a line of spaces at the end of the file"). A real plugin: csvplugin.py 24 KB plus its own AdvancedCSV.tmLanguage (so .csv files open with that syntax), 12 palette commands (csv_format_compact, csv_format_expand, csv_format, csv_sort_by_col_asc/desc, csv_insert_col, csv_delete_col, csv_delete_trailing_cols, csv_select_col, csv_set_delimiter, csv_set_output, csv_evaluate), context menu and keymaps. dependencies.json makes Package Control install the numpy library - it pulled "numpy 2.5.4 for Python 3.14" into Data/Lib and removed it again on uninstall ("Removed orphaned library numpy"). WORKS: csv_format_expand justified three ragged columns to width (name 11, age 3, city 13) with the delimiter kept; csv_sort_by_col_asc and _desc open a quick panel ['Use header row', "Don't use header row"] and, answered with the header option, sorted ann / bartholomew / w and reversed them while keeping the header first. (I drove the quick panel by temporarily patching sublime.Window.show_quick_panel to call the callback with 0 and restored the original in a finally block.) csv_format_compact leaves an already-compact buffer unchanged, which is correct - it strips whitespace rather than padding. DEFECT, same root cause in two places: FromView splits the buffer on "\n", so a file that ends with a newline (the normal case) yields a trailing empty row. Sorting ascending then places that empty row directly after the header - the result was "name,age,city", a blank line, then the three data rows - and csv_format_expand pads it into a line of spaces at EOF. With no trailing newline both artifacts disappear (verified both ways). Upstream issue #58 covers the expand half; the sort blank-line half is the same bug and was not filed (repo dead). Checks: install console delta 3 then 7 lines (numpy library install, plugin reload), 0 errors, no dialogs; command runs produced no dialogs; removal 3 lines including the numpy cleanup; Data/Installed Packages back to Color Scheme - Legacy + Package Control, Data/Lib back to its earlier contents, the on-disk test CSV untouched (65 bytes, changes discarded with the scratch view).

2016.08.02.09.07.56 on 4215 (shagabutdinov; issues at github.com/shagabutdinov/sublime-autocompletion). Four modules - autocompletion.py (the TextCommand), word.py/nesting.py (completion handlers), utility.py (regex helpers) - palette entries "AutocompletionFuzzy: Complete word forward/backward (fuzzy)" and the non-fuzzy variants, keymap ctrl+p/ctrl+o gated on setting.sublime_enhanced_keybindings with an overlay_visible context, and a demo/ pair of .js files. INSTALL ALONE IS BROKEN and says so loudly: nesting.py imports Expression, so Package Control installs the package but the modules fail with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'Expression' (nesting.py line 4, 2 error lines) and Sublime raises a native modal "Dependency import failed; please read readme for Autocompletion plugin for installation instructions; to disable this message remove this plugin; message: No module named 'Expression'". There is no way for the author to declare it in this channel: all 4843 channel entries carry "dependencies": null. Installing the separate channel package Expression (shagabutdinov/sublime-expression, 2018.01.19) and reinstalling AutocompletionFuzzy made all four modules load with 0 errors and no modal. WORKS after that: the command needs explicit args (a bare "autocompletion" does nothing - it requires handler/backward), and with handler AutocompletionFuzzy.word.create_fuzzy_completion, backward false, a buffer "x = alp" followed by alpha_alphabet/beta/gamma_alphanumeric extended the word to alpha_alphabet on the first invocation. Direction matters and is by design: the forward search looks only at text after the caret (text.split at the cursor, plus other views), backward searches before it, so a word at EOF with nothing to its right produces no completion. Checks: install deltas 21 and 8 and 14 console lines with the expected 2 error lines on the first install only; the Expression install was clean; removal of both packages 11 lines, 0 errors, 0 dialogs; views closed as scratch; Data/Installed Packages back to baseline.

0.1.7 on 4215 (installs unpacked because it ships .no-sublime-package). It works by generating a key map rather than by listening to text: plugin_loaded reads default_replacements (65 typo->correction pairs such as teh->the, adn->and, becuase->because), default_triggers (space, enter, comma, period, semicolon, underscore, colon, hyphen) plus the custom_replacements/custom_triggers settings, and rewrites Default.sublime-keymap inside its own package directory with one multi-key binding per correction x trigger x {lowercase, capitalised} - 65 x 8 x 2 = 1040 entries, 109 KB of JSON. The console shows "Building AutoSpell Index: Started/Finished" on every load. WORKS, verified with real keystrokes rather than the API: typing "teh " "adn " "zzqx " into a plain-text view through window input produced exactly "the and zzqx " - both known typos were replaced including the trailing trigger character and the unknown word was left alone. Pasting or API-inserting the same text (run_command append) is NOT corrected, which follows from the design: the correction only fires when the sequence arrives as discrete key presses, so pasted text, IME input and multi-line inserts bypass it. Minor, recorded not filed: the keymap is written into the package directory on every startup (which is why the package must stay unpacked and why the file is 109 KB), and the auto_spell command is a stub that only prints 'run AutoSpell' and has no palette entry - the palette/context menu expose nothing; the README documents editing the settings instead. Rig note: while setting this test up I passed a non-existent syntax path to assign_syntax, which raised a native ST modal ("Error loading syntax file ... Unable ..."); it was dismissed via the window with the computer-use tool and is my error, not the package's. Checks: install console delta 8 lines, 0 errors, no dialogs; removal 2 lines, no dialogs; views closed as scratch, Data/Installed Packages and Data/Packages back to baseline.

1.0.1 on 4215 (int3h; issues at github.com/int3h/sublime-better-javascript - repo DEAD, last commit 2014-10-15, so nothing filed). It ships its own JavaScript.tmLanguage and JSON.tmLanguage plus six Symbol List tmPreferences, two Completion/Comment/Indent tmPreferences and 12 snippets (function, if/else, for loops, console_log, prototype, setTimeout, object helpers). IT HIJACKS THE BUILT-IN SYNTAX: on load, Install.py appends "JavaScript" to ignored_packages in the user's global Preferences.sublime-settings and saves the file, without asking - verified, the file gained "ignored_packages": ["JavaScript", "Vintage"] and settings reported it back. The symbol list itself works and is exactly the advertised improvement: on a sample with a plain function, a var-assigned function, a prototype method and a nested function, view.symbols() returned greet, Thing, "Thing.prototype.doIt", Outer and Inner, i.e. prototype methods are qualified and nested functions are indexed, which the stock JS index does not do. DEFECT, recorded not filed (repo dead): uninstalling does NOT restore the setting. After remove_packages the Preferences file still lists "JavaScript" in ignored_packages, so the built-in JavaScript package stays disabled - opening a .js file then gave syntax "Packages/Text/Plain text.tmLanguage" and scope text.plain, i.e. no JavaScript highlighting at all until the user edits Preferences.by hand. I put ignored_packages back to ["Vintage"] afterwards. Checks: install console delta 6 lines, 0 errors, no dialogs; removal 2 lines, no dialogs; views closed as scratch; Data/Installed Packages back to baseline. After I restored ignored_packages to ["Vintage"] by hand the built-in JavaScript syntax was reachable again in the same session - assign_syntax resolved Packages/JavaScript/JavaScript.tmLanguage - with no restart of Sublime, so the earlier assumption that a relaunch is needed to undo the setting is wrong.

WORKS - version 1.3.1 (2019-10-15), ST4 4215 / Python 3.14.6. Installs and loads with only SyntaxWarning noise (about forty 'invalid escape sequence' warnings from util/vcs.py, parser/file_diff.py and parser/hunk_diff.py; cosmetic, they will become errors in a future Python). Command set is three entries: diff_view (custom diff), diff_view_uncommitted, diff_hunks_list. Proved on a real repo: a git repo with one committed file, then the file edited to change a line and add a function; with that file active, 'Diff View: Show uncommitted changes' opened a two-pane side-by-side diff with a hunk list at the top ('mod.py : 2 def greet(name): 5+/1-'), the old content in the left pane and the new content in the right pane with the changed lines marked. WORKS once its prerequisite exists, but silently does nothing on a plain install - version 0.5.2 (2025-03-28), ST4 4215 / Py 3.14.6. With only this addon installed, a clean restart left its module absent from sys.modules: plugin.py imports 'from SublimeLinter import highlight_view' at module level, while package-metadata.json has dependencies null and there is no dependencies.json, so Package Control installs nothing else and the addon fails to load with nothing shown to the user. With SublimeLinter installed by hand it loads and does exactly what it advertises. Functional proof: a throwaway SublimeLinter linter reporting one error at line 5 col 5 (needs defaults={'selector': ...} or LinterMeta disables the class at registration - worth knowing) was linted into the view, then 'sublime_linter_goto_error' moved the selection from (0,0) to (43,43), i.e. line 5 column 5, and view.get_regions('SL.flash_jump_position.flash') returned exactly [(43,44)] - the flash region drawn at the jumped-to error, using the package's own region key; with 'duration' raised to 30 the region was still readable afterwards, confirming it is removed on a timer at the configured duration. Filed kaste/SublimeLinter-addon-goto-flash#1 for the missing dependency wiring; same root cause as the SublimeLinter-any-lsp issue filed the same day.

FEEDBACK 2026-11-07: kaste answered kaste/SublimeLinter-addon-goto-flash#1 with 'That's like installing a VST plugin without having a DAW.' - i.e. an adapter's prerequisite is self-evident and the missing-dependency report was noise. Accepted without argument: replied in one short paragraph (the narrow point was only that the failure is silent, that is a nicety and his to decide), then closed the issue myself. State of the pair filed the same day: goto-flash#1 CLOSED by us at the author's dismissal; kaste/SublimeLinter-any-lsp#1 left OPEN on purpose, because its reportable part is different - that README says 'Manual only. Not listed on PackageControl' while the package IS listed, a documentation contradiction rather than a missing prerequisite. Lesson written into the skill: before filing a missing-prerequisite report, ask whether the package would make sense without the other package at all; if it would not, only a documentation error can be reportable, and the finding should be recorded rather than filed. The verified evidence from that test stands regardless: the flash region appeared at SL.flash_jump_position.flash [(43,44)] after goto_less error, with duration raised to observe it.

The package loads cleanly and .lua files get the XMake syntax automatically, and it registers ten palette commands plus a build system and completions. Two failures, both reproduced: (1) every command run with no project folder dies in the error path with TypeError: XmakePlugin.console_show() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given at xmake.py line 104 (self.console_show(window) against def console_show(self) at line 76) - hit from both xmake_build (line 457) and xmake_run (line 545); the two guidance lines print first, so the user is told to save a project and then gets a traceback. That one is already known upstream: issue #9, fixed by PR #10 (merged 2026-10-03, self.console_show()), but the fix was never released, so 1.0.6 still carries it. (2) NEW and filed as xmake-io/xmake-sublime#11: with a project open and xmake NOT installed (where xmake finds nothing, no process ever starts), XMake: Build reports 'Build Finished, 0.05 seconds!' in the xmake panel while nothing is built - no .xmake directory, no artifacts, no error anywhere. Cause: run_command() uses subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=PIPE, shell=True) and pipes only stdout into the panel; cmd.exe reports a missing executable on stderr, and process.returncode is never checked, so a total failure is indistinguishable from success. Cosmetic, same palette: 'XMake: Genterate Compile Commands' (Generate).
